Next.js 15.5.20 vendors its own internal postcss@8.4.31 inside node_modules/next/node_modules/postcss. Verified directly: an npm `overrides` entry does not remove this nested copy (Node module resolution still finds Next's own bundled version from within Next's own code), and forcing the override produces an invalid npm dependency tree (`ELSPROBLEMS`) for no actual security benefit. The XSS is in postcss's CSS stringifier and requires attacker-controlled CSS content reaching postcss; this project's own build pipeline only processes static, repository-authored Tailwind source files. Waiting on an upstream Next.js patch release that bumps its internal postcss pin.
